With in-memory data, random access is fast. But with HDF5, reading 10,000 random rows one-by-one is orders of magnitude slower than reading a contiguous slice of 10,000 rows.

**The Fix:**
The `HDF5Matrix.__getitem__` method in `keras/utils/io_utils.py` needs to be optimized. When given a list/array of indices, it should sort them and, if dense enough, read a contiguous hyperslab from the HDF5 file (which is fast) and then re-order/sub-select the needed rows in memory (which is cheap). This would avoid the expensive random-access pattern on the hdf5 dataset.
